metadata.description: Real design-stage Road Safety Audit of McGrath Highway (Route 28) at Mystic Avenue (Route 38) and Broadway (Route 28), Somerville MA; HNTB Corporation for MassDOT Highway Division Safety Section with a multidisciplinary RSA team (meetings December 2016). Converted from the publicly co-published report.
metadata.scheme_summary: Existing urban signalized intersections on the Route 28 corridor under design-stage review for pedestrian, bicycle and vehicle safety enhancements.
metadata.authority: MassDOT Highway Division Safety Section; City of Somerville

project_information_package.value: Design-stage RSA background: two High-Crash-Location-class signalized intersections on the Route 28 corridor reviewed by a multidisciplinary RSA team per FHWA RSA process.

design_drawings_current_phase.value: Existing geometries and conditions presented to the RSA team for both intersections (crash history and speed regulations provided in advance).

crash_history.value: Crash history summaries supplied to participants in advance for Route 28/Broadway and Route 28/Route 38.

expected_findings_baseline.location: McGrath Highway/Broadway intersection — pedestrian signals and crossings
expected_findings_baseline.scenario: The RSA records existing dysfunctional pedestrian signals at McGrath Highway/Broadway: pedestrians relying on those displays may receive no or contradictory guidance while crossing a high-volume urban arterial at the design stage under review.

statement.text: Investigate and fix existing dysfunctional pedestrian signals before the design progresses so pedestrian indications provide reliable guidance at McGrath Highway/Broadway.

evidence.quote: Investigate and fix existing dysfunctional pedestrian signals.

confidence.label: high
confidence.basis: The signal deficiency is recorded directly in the sample report's safety-issue table for McGrath Highway/Broadway; the exposure scenario is derived reasoning about pedestrians relying on the displays.

expected_findings_baseline.rationale: ORCH-as-judge baseline derived from the recorded safety issue and its listed enhancement; distinguishable from quoted evidence, which supplies the recorded deficiency itself.
expected_findings_baseline.recommendation: Investigate and fix existing dysfunctional pedestrian signals as part of the current design stage.

expected_findings_baseline.location: All pedestrian crossings at both audited intersections
expected_findings_baseline.scenario: The RSA's enhancement list calls for updating all pedestrian crossings — crosswalk markings, pedestrian refuge island size, detectable warning panels, APS push buttons and countdown signals — to comply with AAB/ADA Standards. Whether current provisions meet those standards is a normative conformance question recorded as requiring update work; it is categorically distinct from any safety judgment.

statement.text: Update all pedestrian crossings to comply with AAB/ADA Standards, including crosswalk markings, pedestrian refuge island size, detectable warning panels, APS push buttons and countdown signals.
statement.normative_basis_note: AAB/ADA Standards apply to pedestrian access elements at these public intersections; the audit records an update-to-comply entry rather than a determination.

evidence.quote: Update all pedestrian crossings to comply with AAB/ADA Standards (update crosswalk markings, pedestrian refuge island size, detectable warning panels, APS push buttons and countdown signals).

confidence.label: high
confidence.basis: The enhancement-list entry is recorded verbatim in the sample report; treated as a compliance question because AAB/ADA Standards are mandatory instruments, with the update entry indicating non-conforming elements without asserting a regulatory verdict.

expected_findings_baseline.rationale: ORCH-as-judge baseline framed as a compliance question per the judge-feedback categorical line: the sample supplies an update-to-comply prescription, not a safety finding.
expected_findings_baseline.recommendation: Update all pedestrian crossings to comply with AAB/ADA Standards within the current design.
